sections.overview: This sandgrouse spans arid lands from the Sahel to South Asia.
sections.identification: Long central tail feathers and a black belly mark it in flight.
sections.habitat: It uses open desert and stony country; in Israel it nests in the Negev.
sections.diet: Regional sources report a diet of seeds and sprouts.
sections.behavior: It is sociable and visits water; populations may be resident or nomadic.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground; both sexes incubate in shifts.
sections.ecology: Compare it with the southern African Namaqua and clay-grassland Yellow-throated Sandgrouse.
sections.conservation: BirdLife classifies it globally as Least Concern.
